It is the only item in the batch where ん precedes や/vowel, so the rule applies here specifically. Fix to hon'yaku (standard dictionary form).

The disputed 'por aqui (área)' includes an explicit '(área)' parenthetical that disambiguates it from the literal deictic 'around here', defusing the 'misleads' claim. 辺 is overwhelmingly used in この辺/その辺, giving the 'por aqui' flavor real pedagogical value. Corpus house style already mixes such locational glosses into noun entries (cf. sibling 近く/vocab:1242160 pt 'proximidades, redondezas, perto'). Minor/stylistic, finding confidence only 0.6.

Defensible for a learner dictionary. 辺 is almost never used bare; it appears overwhelmingly in この辺/その辺/あの辺, where the phrase genuinely conveys 'around here/there', so 'por aqui (área)' reflects real usage a learner will encounter. The parenthetical '(área)' explicitly anchors it to a location rather than pure deixis, preventing the claimed 'teaches 辺 alone means around here' harm. The other two glosses (redondeza, arredores) are correct pt-BR nouns delivering the core sense. The POS/register concern is a minor stylistic quibble, not something false or below professional quality.

Defensible. 沖 does mean the waters off the coast, and 'largo' is a genuine Portuguese maritime noun ('o largo' = alto-mar / the sea away from shore), so 'largo da costa' is not false. The two primary glosses ('alto-mar', 'mar aberto') already carry the sense clearly and idiomatically; in that parallel context the third gloss reads as another sea-noun, not the adjective 'wide'. The suggested 'ao largo da costa' is an adverbial/prepositional idiom ('off the coast'), a worse POS match for the noun 沖, so the fix isn't clearly better. Minor stylistic polish, not a defect.

Primary gloss 'injeção' is exactly correct for 注射 and carries the core sense. Nothing false is taught. The proposed fix 'dose (de vacina)' is worse — 'dose' denotes a quantity of medication, not the act of injecting, and also narrows to vaccine. Defensible for a learner dictionary; low-confidence style nitpick.
